summary: The first draft has 134 screens in 20 groups, built on Journey's design system (Sun, glass, Plus Jakarta Sans, the same components). Two things you decided on 12 Nov are now in: **Notes keeps its name**, and **Health is in the first version**. Health is the seventh place, for every kind of circle, and the kind of circle chosen at setup shapes what it gets, with a full set drawn for couples, housemates and friends beside the family one. Nothing is built yet.
next: Health is in the first version, so its legal check now has a date: tell me which countries you will launch in first, and who should look at it. It has to be finished before the Health step is built.

Look at the newest groups at the end of the **Screens**: 17 *Health*, 18 *For couples*, 19 *For housemates*, 20 *For friends*, and the two new setup screens (2.5 and 2.6). Tell me what to keep, what to drop and what is missing for each kind of circle.

If you haven't yet: groups 14 to 16 (*Jot*, *Keepsakes*, *Fair and fun*), then the rest of the **Screens**. Group 10, *With Journey*, and the sheet screens in group 8 are the ones I most want your eye on.
Try the names for the app with the **Name** switch on the Screens page, then read *The name*.
Answer the eight questions under *What it does*. Two of them shape the build most: how private is private, and whether there is a paid plan.
To let me reply inside a comment thread and close it, send the thread to Claude (reply on it with Send to Claude). Your first three are answered by groups 14 to 16 but stay open until then.

open.a: You've put Health in the first version, so this is no longer whether but when. Health details are a protected kind of personal data, and app stores set their own conditions for apps that hold them. The screens stay on the safe side (records and reminders, no advice). A check by someone qualified has to finish before the Health step is built. Which countries first, and who does it?

An iPhone will not keep a notification for ever or take typing inside a widget; an Android phone does more. I drew what each can really do: on iPhone a pinned note you press and hold to type in (it returns after each add), one-tap chips and ticks in widgets, voice, the Action Button and the share sheet. Is that close enough to what you pictured, or should the iPhone side lean harder on one of them?
My pick is Porchlight. Hearth would have been perfect and is taken by a family organiser. None of the names has had a trademark, store or domain check yet.

In this draft the Vault and Health's records are scrambled so that the service can't read them. Pages, photos and files are private to the people you choose but readable by the service, so that search inside scans, reminders from documents and moments can work. Scrambling everything is possible and switches those off.
Keeping a family's full-size photos and videos costs roughly US$0.75 to 3 a month per family. A free amount with a family plan is the usual answer. The numbers are yours to set.

open.q: What else is in the first version?
open.a: Health is in, by your decision. That brings the Vault's locked storage in with it, because Health's records are kept the same way. My suggested order: circles and sharing, Library, Plan with Jot, Notes, Money, Vault, Health, then the links with Journey. Does anything wait for a second version?
Today, Plan, Notes, Library, Money, Health, Vault. Seven is all the row holds. Are these the right seven, in the right order? Is anything you'd use daily more than one tap away?
Grouping photos by who is in them is powerful and sensitive, most of all with children. On the phone only, off by default, or not at all? The draft leaves it out.
Send a booking, a bill or a school letter to the circle's own address and it arrives as an event or a bill. It needs a mail-receiving service that Journey doesn't have. First version, or later?

updates.text: Two decisions from you. **Notes keeps its name**: Lore is gone from every screen. **Health is in the first version**: it now has its own step in the build order, straight after the Vault whose locked storage it uses, and its legal check moves to the top of the next steps.

Three changes you asked for, 37 more screens. **Lore** is the new name for Notes. **Health** (11 screens) is the seventh place, for every circle: who gave the medicine, a sick day written down, the emergency card, moving together, and more. **A circle's kind** now shapes what it gets: two new setup screens, and a full set each for **couples**, **housemates** and **friends** (8 screens apiece: their Home, their templates, three keepsakes, three small rituals).

After your first three comments: 22 more screens. **Jot** (8): widgets, a note pinned in notifications that you type into, voice, the share button, and how each phone's limits are handled. **Keepsakes** (7): Open when…, the birthday interview, Things they said, Same spot every year, Grandma's stories, the good things jar, the doorframe. **Fair and fun** (6): Whose turn?, the piggy bank, secret missions, the Saturday jar, Sleeps until…, Where is it?. Plus *Goodnight from far away* in the Journey group.

First draft: the hub, 75 screens in 13 groups, the design system copied from Journey's Design 2.1, a name shortlist with a switch on every screen, the link with Journey, the requirements, and the answer on sharing a database and a server.
